question: In which year did the Government of India introduce Securities Transaction Tax (STT) to reduce the complexities involved in the taxation of securities transactions, promote fair trading, and prevent market manipulation?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**2004**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Securities Transaction Tax (STT)** was introduced by the **Government of India** in the year **2004**.
 
• The primary objective of STT is to simplify the taxation of securities transactions and ensure **transparency** in the trading process.
 
• It is a tax levied on the purchase and sale of securities such as **shares, equity-oriented mutual funds, and derivatives**.
 
• This tax is collected at the source by the **stock exchanges**, which makes it easier for the government to monitor and enforce compliance.
 
• The introduction of STT was aimed at curbing **market manipulation** and promoting **fair trading practices**.
 
• Unlike capital gains tax, STT is applicable irrespective of whether the transaction results in a profit or loss.
 
• It is governed under the provisions of the **Income Tax Act, 1961**.
 
• STT has contributed significantly to creating a more efficient and streamlined tax collection system for securities transactions.
